title: USA I Media Visa from the UK | Journalist Visa Help
description: USA I media visa for journalists and media professionals working in the USA, where an ESTA can’t be used. Help from Manchester advisers.
h1: USA I media visa from the UK
intro: The I visa is for journalists, film crews and other media professionals working in the USA for a foreign media organisation. Media work generally can’t be done on an ESTA. We prepare your I media visa application and check every detail before it is submitted.

sections.heading: Who needs an I visa?
sections.text: Reporters, editors, camera crews and other media staff travelling to the USA to gather news or make information programmes for a non-US media organisation need an I visa. Using an ESTA for media work can lead to being refused entry.

sections.heading: The US visa interview
sections.text: Most US visas involve the online DS-160 form, paying the visa fee, and an interview at the US Embassy in London or the US Consulate in Belfast. Every answer on the DS-160 must be accurate and match your documents. We prepare your form and tell you what to take to the interview.

sections.heading: I media visa help from Manchester
sections.text: We're based in Manchester city centre and help travellers and businesses across the UK. We check the rules for your passport, prepare your application and keep you updated until it's decided.

faqs.a: Generally not for media work. Journalists working in the USA need an I visa.
A letter from your media employer describing your role and assignment, plus press credentials if you have them.

faqs.q: How long does a I media visa take?
faqs.a: Processing times vary with the authority and the time of year. Apply as early as you can, and don’t book non-refundable travel until your visa or authorisation is approved.

faqs.q: Can you help with my I media visa application?
faqs.a: Yes. We check which visa fits your trip, prepare your I media visa application and documents, and keep you updated. Contact us or call 0161 956 2003.
